ri_fortress_of_solitude.blurb: A small bouldering zone on the Connors Farm hillside in northern Rhode Island, tucked into the Fortress Area alongside a lone neighbouring boulder. It holds 17 problems on granite, and the character is steep: a cave and a bulging face give the best lines, so expect power and overhanging moves rather than slab. The spread leans hard, with a couple of easy warm-ups, a handful in the V3 range, and most of the rest between V5 and V8, so it suits climbers who already boulder at a solid level. The problems carry Superman-themed names. Trails to the boulders are short, and a few minutes of walking from the lot puts you at the cave.

ut_all_thumbs_boulder.blurb: One of the larger boulders on the Secret Garden trail, down at the lower end of Little Cottonwood Canyon in the Wasatch. It carries 17 problems with a wide range: four or so easy V0 lines suitable for beginners or a warm-up, a solid middle band from V2 to V5, and a few tougher problems topped by the V10 that gives the boulder its name. The north face holds a well-liked easy line that works for newer boulderers, while the harder lines on the other sides draw stronger climbers. As part of one of the busiest bouldering zones in the canyon, it sees steady traffic, and a short trail walk from the road reaches it.

ut_frontera_the.blurb: A compact, steep wall of bolted routes beside the road in Maple Canyon, central Utah, right by the forest boundary sign. Seventeen sport lines cover a broad spread: a pair of easy fives, a mid-grade group around 5.9 to 5.11, and a stronger set in the 5.12s and low 5.13s, so both newer and experienced sport climbers find something. The wall is small, which keeps things quick and social, and the car sits only a few steps from the base. The cobble-studded canyon rock encourages pocket and jug pulling on steep terrain.

ut_mars.blurb: A cliff band along the Potash Road corridor outside Moab, holding 17 routes on dark red sandstone. Most of the climbs are bolted sport lines, with three trad routes mixed in. Walls are vertical with some overhanging stretches, and the lines run roughly 40 to 95 feet. Grades start around 5.9 and top out in the low 5.12s, with the bulk sitting in the 5.10 and 5.11 range, so it fits intermediate to strong climbers best. A trail leads to the base, a walk of roughly a quarter hour from the road via the same approach used for a neighbouring crag, then right along the cliff band.

ut_ripple.blurb: A cluster of 17 sandstone boulder problems in Moe's Valley outside St. George, sitting just northeast of the Tee Pee boulder in the Tee Pee Area. The spread is wide: a few easy V1 and V2 problems, a solid mid-range around V4 to V6, and some serious tests in the V7 to V9 band, plus one very hard problem at the top. Mr. Rippler, Underwhere and Jibber are among the most-climbed. Moe's Valley is a popular winter bouldering destination, and this corner is reached by a walk of up to about fifteen minutes from the end of the road.

ut_election_wall_2.blurb: A short, fairly moderate wall in Indian Creek, southeast Utah, holding 17 trad routes on sandstone. Lines are on the brief side and run mostly between 5.10 and 5.11, with a single 5.12-. About half sit at 5.10, which makes it a reasonable stop for climbers building up to the tougher walls in the Creek, though it still demands solid crack technique. One route, Stairway to Heaven, stretches to three pitches while the rest are single pitch. The wall is described as sunny, and a cairned trail from a parking area leads up to the base.
